headline: Switching to {arm:f64} cuts cost per reply by {cost.uplift.f64|abs|pct} but loses {contrast.f64.persona.delta|abs|pts} points of in-character rate, mostly in long conversations.
lede: The loss grows with depth: past ten turns, {arm:f64} holds character far less often than {control.name}, while short conversations are close. A blind preference test or a live hybrid would show whether users notice before the savings are taken.

slots.text: {arm:f64} costs {cost.uplift.f64|abs|pct} less per reply than {control.name} and loses {contrast.f64.persona.delta|abs|pts} points of in-character rate ({contrast.f64.persona.interval|pts}). It holds every guardrail; {arm:f16} and {arm:cor} each break one.

The answer turns on what one point of in-character rate is worth per month. Below the price where the savings equal the loss, {arm:f64} wins; above it, {control.name} does. Set the price in the explore part to see the flip.

Our lean: a hybrid that serves early turns with {arm:f64} and hands longer conversations back to {control.name}. It keeps most of the savings and avoids most of the loss, but it is modeled, not measured.
A two-week live test of the hybrid on a slice of traffic, watching session length and thumbs-down rate in conversations past five turns, where raters already lean toward {control.name}.

method.text: Conversations replayed from September logs; every arm answered the same user turns, so differences are paired.
A judge with the persona rubric, calibrated on {judged.persona.calibration_ratings|int} human-rated replies (agreement {judged.persona.agreement|pct}).
Standing policy, not set for this campaign: declines to speculate and music facts correct. Options that break one are shown but left out of the pricing unless included.
Modeled, not run: the cheaper model serves early turns and Production the rest, weighted by the share of replies at each depth.
Measured tokens times list price per thousand replies, at {meta.volume_per_month|int} replies a month.

flag.title: No rule set in advance.
flag.text: The campaign did not say how much personality a dollar is worth, so this page prices the trade instead of deciding it. The persona's owner makes the call; the measured changes stand as shown.

sections.headline: Personality is the only judged loss for {arm:f64}; {arm:f16} also gets music facts wrong more often
sections.takeaway: Change in points against {control.name} on the same conversations, for the two judged aspects. A whisker clear of zero is a real change.

sections.headline: The flash models hold character for a few turns, then drift
sections.takeaway: In-character rate by how deep into the conversation the reply is. Short conversations are close; the gap opens past five turns.

sections.headline: Raters prefer Production clearly only in longer conversations
sections.takeaway: Blind side-by-side ratings of {control.name} against {arm:f64}. Right of the middle means raters preferred {control.name}.
sections.caption: This is the only link between the judge's points and what people notice, and it is small: read it as direction, not size.
